bug_semantics: The api/api.py /api/wiki_cache endpoints (GET read, POST save, DELETE delete) build the on-disk cache file path directly from user-controlled query/body fields: get_wiki_cache_path(owner, repo, repo_type, language) formats them into `f"deepwiki_cache_{repo_type}_{owner}_{repo}_{language}.json"` and joins onto WIKI_CACHE_DIR with os.path.join, with NO sanitization. Because os.path.join discards everything before an absolute component and the fields are never checked for '..', '..', '/', leading '/' or absolute forms, an unauthenticated remote attacker controls the joined path: os.remove(cache_path) in delete_wiki_cache deletes ARBITRARY FILES (e.g. owner='../../../../' + target file, or absolute /etc/... in a field), and read_wiki_cache/save_wiki_cache likewise read/write attacker-chosen paths — arbitrary file write/delete with the API process's (in deployments, root) privileges (CWE-22). DELETE additionally guards only an optional static authorization_code (WIKI_AUTH_MODE off by default); the GET endpoint has no auth at all.
flaw_origin: Commit 36d7fa915ecb08f4b19123796ee4af95c1a0eb2c ("Move localstorage cache from browser to server side. Cached generated wiki content", 2025-05-08, author/committer davideuler <davideuler@github.com>) first wrote the vulnerable sink: it introduced get_wiki_cache_path() with the unsanitized f-string + os.path.join construction and the GET/POST /api/wiki_cache endpoints consuming user-controlled owner/repo/repo_type/language. The advisory's named sink — 'wiki-cache endpoint constructs file paths from user-controlled owner, repo, and repo_type fields without sanitization' — is born in this commit; no prior server-side wiki-cache path construction existed. The follow-up commit 9df12b238312 (2025-05-09, davideuler) added the DELETE variant with os.remove() on the same unsanitized path, completing the arbitrary-delete primitive named in the advisory; recorded in decomposed_shas.

evidence: Advisory (CVE-2026-72567 / GHSA-r232-48q8-3598): AsyncFuncAI/deepwiki-open through commit 16f35a0 — improper path validation lets unauthenticated remote attackers write to or delete arbitrary files with root privileges; api/api.py wiki-cache endpoint constructs file paths from user-controlled owner, repo, repo_type without sanitization (CWE-22).

Sink at advisory floor: `git show 16f35a0:api/api.py` — :405 WIKI_CACHE_DIR, :408-411 `def get_wiki_cache_path(...): filename = f"deepwiki_cache_{repo_type}_{owner}_{repo}_{language}.json"; return os.path.join(WIKI_CACHE_DIR, filename)`; :477 read via that path (no auth); :428 save; :504-540 DELETE endpoint with `cache_path = get_wiki_cache_path(owner, repo, repo_type, language)` then `os.remove(cache_path)`. No '..' filtering, no basename extraction, no startswith/commonpath containment check anywhere in the file.

BIC introduction: `git log -S 'get_wiki_cache_path' -- api/api.py --all` → introduced by 36d7fa915ecb08f4b19123796ee4af95c1a0eb2c (2025-05-08, davideuler, parent 9f76ddd1f58f); `git show 36d7fa91:api/api.py` already contains the identical unsanitized f-string join (:276-279) plus the consuming endpoints. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 36d7fa91 16f35a0` → True (BIC ancestor of advisory floor). DELETE primitive added by 9df12b238312 (2025-05-09), also ancestor of 16f35a0.

potential_fix.approach: Canonicalize and jail generated output paths under a dedicated cache root with realpath checks before any file write or delete in /api/wiki_cache.
potential_fix.rationale: Path jailing prevents attacker-controlled identifiers from escaping the cache directory to arbitrary write/delete targets.
